Augustus.text: Augustus owns half of the Hat Creek Cattle Company in the dusty border town of Lonesome Dove. A talkative, whiskey-sipping Tennessean and former Ranger, he loves a good argument, eats enormous meals, and prefers thinking in the shade to hard work. He alone seems able to tease his stern partner, Captain Call, down to size.

Pea Eye.text: Pea Eye is a tall, gangly hand at the Hat Creek Cattle Company and a former Ranger corporal who still follows Captain Call's lead. Slow to think but skilled at careful jobs like smithing and carpentry, he is half deaf in one ear from an old fight with the Keechis. He works the lots at Lonesome Dove.

Call.text: Captain Woodrow Call is Augustus's partner in the Hat Creek Cattle Company at Lonesome Dove, and a former Ranger captain. Scottish-born and only middle-sized, he still has a way of seeming bigger than he is. Tireless, terse and disapproving of idle talk, he keeps a stylish but vicious mare and plans night raids across the Rio Grande.

Bolivar.text: Bolivar is the Hat Creek outfit's elderly cook in Lonesome Dove, a retired Mexican bandit who crossed the river once his old trade grew crowded. Fiercely independent, he serves endless beans and suspiciously acquired goat, lives mostly on sugary coffee, and pounds the dinner bell with a crowbar whenever it suits him, whatever the men think.

Newt.text: Newt is the youngest hand at the Hat Creek Cattle Company, a teenage horse wrangler who digs wells and dodges Captain Call's mean mare. Good-natured and fond of the pigs, he longs to be old enough to wear a gun and ride along on the outfit's nighttime raids into Mexico across the river.

Lorena.text: Lorena Wood lives above the Dry Bean, the saloon in Lonesome Dove, where she earns her living as a prostitute after a gambler abandoned her in town a few months back. Thought to have the most beautiful face the town has ever seen, she is silently adored by young Newt, who has never yet dared to speak to her.

Lippy.text: Lippy is an old man who plays piano at the Dry Bean saloon in Lonesome Dove, though a hole in his stomach makes it hard to keep up. He is one of the few people Lorena will talk with, despite being something of a bother to her, and he urges her to seek her fortune across the river in Mexico.

Xavier Wanz.text: Xavier Wanz owns the Dry Bean, the only saloon in Lonesome Dove and the only place in town that serves food. When Lorena arrived stranded and penniless, he agreed to let her work as the saloon's cook until the wary local cowboys warmed up to her.

Dish Boggett.text: Dish Boggett is a skilled young cowboy of about twenty-two whose big walrus mustache makes him look older and more solemn. Back in Lonesome Dove after delivering horses to Matamoros and gambling away his pay, he is hopelessly smitten with Lorena. He plans to leave next week with Shanghai Pierce's trail outfit.

Deets.text: Deets is a Black man who has ridden with Call and Augustus almost as long as Pea Eye has. Steady and dependable enough that Call says you could set a clock by him, he was sent to San Antonio to deposit the outfit's money and now rides back toward Lonesome Dove on a big white gelding with an unexpected companion.

Jake Spoon.text: Jake Spoon is an old friend of Call and Augustus, recognized from afar by his habit of slumping to one side in the saddle. He appears without warning on the stage road from San Antonio, riding a pacing bay beside Deets toward Lonesome Dove, and his arrival startles both partners.

July Johnson.text: July Johnson is the young but determined sheriff of Fort Smith, Arkansas. His brother, the town's dentist and mayor, was recently killed by a stray shot from Jake Spoon while July was away in Missouri testifying against stage robbers. Jake, who fled, hopes the sheriff stays too busy to follow him.

Chick.text: Chick is a tiny, pockmarked cowboy with a big pistol and a swaybacked horse who rides into Lonesome Dove with Wilbarger. Crude and quick to cackle, he goes around asking for the town's brothel and the yellow-haired girl he has heard about, until Dish sends him off with a tall tale.

Wilbarger.text: Wilbarger is a stocky, red-faced cattleman about Call's age who rides a handsome black horse. After Mexican raiders stole nearly all his horses, he arrives at the Hat Creek outfit in Lonesome Dove wanting to buy forty, since he has a herd gathered beyond the Nueces bound for Kansas. He is brusque and sharp-tongued.

Sean O'Brien.text: Sean O'Brien is a young, stout Irishman, about Newt's age, who is lost with his older brother Allen at an abandoned wranglers' camp in Mexico. Hungry and quarrelsome but blessed with a fine singing voice, he makes a comic dash to escape on a hobbled mule before Call promises to send horses back for them.

Allen O'Brien.text: Allen O'Brien is a balding, good-humored Irishman stranded with his younger brother Sean at a burnt-out horse camp in Mexico, far from Galveston, where they meant to go. Courteous even when hungry, he treasures their weary mule and misses potatoes. Call promises to send horses back so the brothers can escape.

Jasper Fant.text: Jasper Fant is a skinny cowboy working along the Rio Grande who comes into the Dry Bean in Lonesome Dove to seek Lorena's company. When she simply stares him down in silence, he backs away embarrassed, and through him word spreads among the river cowboys that she no longer takes customers.

Pete Spettle.text: Pete Spettle is the oldest of a poor widow's eight barefoot children, raised on a struggling creek-bottom farm north of Pickles Gap. Only a year older than his brother Bill, he has already helped trail a small herd to Arkansas. Hired by Call for the drive, the brothers set out on foot for Lonesome Dove.

Jimmy Rainey.text: Jimmy Rainey is one of the two oldest sons of Joe and Maude Rainey, whose noisy, well-fed ranch family numbers a dozen children. After Call enjoys a huge supper at their place, Maude promises that Jimmy and his brother Ben will report to Lonesome Dove by week's end. The boy himself barely says a word.

Bill Spettle.text: Bill Spettle, called Swift Bill, is a boy about Newt's age from a desperately poor family farm north of Pickles Gap, where his widowed mother is raising eight children. Hired by Call along with his older brother Pete, he walks toward Lonesome Dove carrying a blanket and the family's one battered pistol.

Ben Rainey.text: Ben Rainey is among the eldest sons of the large, lively Rainey family, who feed Call a hearty meal at their ranch. Maude, his outspoken and generous mother, tells Call that Ben and his younger brother Jimmy will ride over to Lonesome Dove within days to sign on. Both boys stay shy and quiet in the Captain's presence.

Needle Nelson.text: Needle Nelson is a tall cowboy from north of San Antonio who turns up in Lonesome Dove looking for work with the Hat Creek outfit. Wire-thin, with a very large Adam's apple, he gathers and brands cattle by day, plays cards at night, and frets that the drive is starting too late.

Bert Borum.text: Bert Borum is a cheerful cowboy from Brownsville who hires on with the Hat Creek outfit as it gathers and brands cattle near Lonesome Dove. Quick to laugh and pleasant to hear, he finds nearly everything funny and jokes about tying jugs to his horse as floats for the river crossings ahead.

Soupy Jones.text: Soupy Jones is a short former Ranger who once served briefly with Call and Augustus, known as a fine cardplayer and the best horseman any of them has seen. Recently widowed in Bastrop, he rides into the Hat Creek camp at dawn, partly curious about his old friend Jake, and is hired for the drive.
